The AI Semiconductor Boom and What Could End It with Stacy Rasgon | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 63

Stacy Rasgon describes AI demand spreading from GPUs into CPU, memory, networking and equipment bottlenecks. He upgrades AMD, remains constructive on Broadcom and NVIDIA, and distinguishes Intel's improved narrative from proven manufacturing economics. Eisman owns NVIDIA and endorses the continuing infrastructure cycle. They reject simplistic immediate GPU obsolescence while identifying weak eventual returns and power limits as risks. Later supplier earnings support demand acceleration, but long-horizon revenue, EPS and investment-return claims remain open.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

  • The $600 AMD warrant threshold is a vesting condition, not an unconditional price target.

Source · 24:08-24:44 ↗
SpeakerSteve Eisman
Stanceasserted
Horizonnot stated
Materialitymajor

The conditional relationship follows from the explicit assumptions; it does not establish that those assumptions hold in observed markets.

Conditional reasoning

Annual expense is depreciable cost divided by useful life. A longer life reduces current expense and increases current pretax profit, while lifetime total depreciation is unchanged. Economic validity requires evidence about useful service life.

  • Straight-line depreciation, unchanged depreciable cost and residual value, no offsetting impairment.

How he reasons here

  • Distinguish earnings revisions from multiple expansion.
  • Inspect bottlenecks across the entire supply chain.
  • Treat reported margin changes separately from impairment base effects.
  • Use GPU rental prices and utilization to assess useful life.
  • Separate temporary digestion from permanent ROI failure.
  • Treat management language, warrants and capex announcements as evidence requiring interpretation.
